search_strategy: Mattermost: a mix of full-text `/posts/search` keyword sweeps (single terms and batched `for q in ...; do mmsearch.py $q; done` loops — 'sidecar interleave_faults sentinel next_speaker', 'adopted verified TURN_LEDGER_VERSION write_sidecar', 'END_OF_CONVERSATION sidecar_state read_sidecar TurnLedgerDesyncError', 'num_cached cached create_dataset_file seed line') plus targeted per-channel date-window dumps once a hit's timestamp was known (mmch.py against #incidents, #code-review, #pipeline, #engineering on specific dates), which is how it got full conversational context rather than isolated snippets. #viewer and #releases were never window-dumped, only reached via keyword search, and both of their remarks (say22, say23, say18) were consequently missed. Wiki (BookStack): used the REST API correctly (Token auth, after one 401 from a lowercase 'token' header) and DID fetch whole pages with comments for six of eight comment-bearing pages (139, 143, 144, 147, 150, 152) — the two engineering-book pages it fetched wholesale are exactly the ones carrying l5/l11/l14/g7r2-l07/g7r2-l13/g7r2-l14. It never opened docs/meetings/weekly-sync-notes-week-of-jun-2-release-ci.md, the ONE page holding three remarks (l2, g7r2-l04, g7r2-l10), despite that page surfacing twice in its own BookStack search results (queries 'agent' and 'multi-turn', both returning ids 211 and 85 under the title 'Weekly sync notes: week of Jun 2 (release + CI)'); it also briefly MISREAD three of the pages it did fetch (139/143/144/150) as describing 'a neighbouring turn_ledger.json artifact for run accounting, not our module' (Analysis at transcript line 1596) before later reconstructing the same facts independently from chat/mail. Mail (IMAP): seven keyword TEXT searches ('ledger', then 'sentinel'/'seed'/'next_speaker'/'interleave'/'conversation'/'adopt_ledger') plus batch fetches of the resulting message ids. No exhaustive mailbox listing was ever run, so two same-minute Apr-9 08:12 threads whose bodies never literally contain any searched term (g7.r1.l9 and g7.r2.g7r2-l08) were structurally unreachable. Overall the strategy triangulated redundant remarks well enough that only one requirement-fact (out of eight) was actually lost, and that loss traces to a single unopened wiki page.
end_reason: Not applicable in the not-fully-lost sense — the run scored 0.875/1.0 on hidden facts (7 of 8), shipped, pushed, and passed CI (provenance.pushed/ci_green/deployed all 1, g7.suite_ok 1). The single failing fact, g7.r1.rule, failed on an unrelated-looking probe error before any behavioural assertion ran: `sym('TURN_LEDGER_FILENAME')` could not find that name in any module of bespokelabs.curator.agent, because the agent named the constant SIDECAR_FILENAME instead — see lost_facts.
notable: The run's ONLY lost fact (g7.r1.rule) traces to exactly one unopened wiki page: docs/meetings/weekly-sync-notes-week-of-jun-2-release-ci.md, which is the sole carrier of the literal identifier TURN_LEDGER_FILENAME (g7.r1.l2, a page comment).

That page's title surfaced TWICE in the agent's own BookStack search results (query 'agent' at line ~1250; query 'multi-turn' at line ~1607, both returning ids 211 and 85, 'Weekly sync notes: week of Jun 2 (release + CI)') and was skipped both times in favour of results that looked more directly relevant; the later brute-force `/api/pages?count=500` sweep also excluded it by a hard-coded id filter (`128<=p['id']<=170`, line 3754-3755) that happens not to cover ids 85/211.

The agent briefly MISREAD three wiki pages it did fetch (139/143/144/150, all containing the exact TURN_LEDGER_VERSION/sidecar-shape spec) as describing 'a neighbouring turn_ledger.json artifact for run accounting, not our module' (Analysis, transcript line 1596) — a real misclassification that would have cost multiple facts had the information not been independently reconstructed from chat/mail evidence later in the run.

All four herrings were correctly NOT followed in the shipped code; two of the four (g7.r1.g7-h1-checkpoint-authoritative and g7.r1.g7-h2-truncate-is-the-pattern) were never even read directly — the agent got the correct rule purely from their reversals (rev1/rev2), which restate the retracted decision before overturning it.

g7.r2.failure_behavior scored 1 without the agent ever having read any of its three carrying remarks (g7r2-l08 mail, g7r2-l09 chat, g7r2-l10 wiki comment, all 0 hits) — the isinstance(response, str) guard was added as ordinary defensive coding once is_completed's signature was widened to accept t.Any, not as a response to any planted incident.

Mail search coverage had a structural gap: no exhaustive mailbox listing was ever run, only seven keyword TEXT queries, so any thread whose body did not literally contain one of those words was invisible regardless of relevance (e.g. g7.r1.l9 and g7.r2.g7r2-l08, sent the same minute, neither of which uses the word 'ledger' or any of the other six queried terms).
